concepts.explanation: So śhāstra is pronounced ‘shaastra’; kṣhīra is ‘ksheera’.  Consonants with a dot below them (ḍ, ṭ and ṇ mainly) are ‘hard’, i.e. pronounced by hitting the tongue on the palate; without a dot, they are soft, with the tongue on the teeth. (As a rough comparison, in the preceding English word ‘teeth’, the first ‘t’ is hard, while the final ‘th’ is soft.) Examples of hard consonants: Āryabhaṭa, gaṇa, paṭhana (studying), pīṭha, goṣṭhī (association, assembly), dhanāḍhya (rich), aṇu (atom).  Finally, ṛ is the Devanagari letter ऋ.
